answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with slashable stake: to earn voting weight each agent locks collateral, so influence follows capital, not the count of identities. Spawning thousands of fake agents grants no extra power because every new identity needs its own deposit. Picture a terrace of onyx kiosks joined by one narrow bridge: a crowd of clones still crosses one at a time, each paying the toll. To sway a vote an attacker must lock a large share of total stake, and any double-vote is slashed, so the cost scales with the influence sought.
